correctness.rationale: For all compact convex planar bodies, the random cyclic gap beta law gives the exact area correlation formula. Positivity of the sine-beta weights follows from integration by parts, and a strict cosine-multiple inequality plus speed-one Parseval produces the nonnegative spectral deficit and equality rigidity. On C4 convex boundaries, a global seventh-order sine remainder is dominated by fourth-derivative Parseval, and Frenet identities produce the exact curvature-cube term with O(m^-6). A separate standard-library checker passed 184 finite diagnostics; the analytic proof, not numerical sampling, establishes infinite/all-m assertions.

value.rationale: A sharp expected-area upper bound for every finite number of boundary samples is strictly stronger than the classical area isoperimetric inequality applied after convex-hull inclusion. The nonnegative Fourier decomposition identifies all equality and geometric shape modes, and the curvature-cube correction isolates the first shape-dependent term in a universal leading-order asymptotic. This answers two natural stochastic geometry questions rather than computing an arbitrary slice.
